A Young diagram is called wide if any subdiagram, formed by a subset of its rows, dominates its conjugate.
Chow et al. [Advances in Applied Mathematics, 31, 2003] conjectured that any wide Young diagram is Latin.
We introduce a notion of an allocation which can be thought of

1 Introduction




Young diagrams are a way of representing partitions of natural numbers. Given a partition n=l1+l2+⋯+lmn=l_{1}+l_{2}+\cdots+l_{m} of a number nn, where 0⩽l1⩽l2⩽⋯⩽lm0\leqslant l_{1}\leqslant l_{2}\leqslant\cdots\leqslant l_{m}, the corresponding Young diagram YY is formed by mm rows of squares that are left-aligned, where the ii-th row from the bottom consists of lil_{i} squares.
Chow, Fan, Goemans, and Vondrak posed the following question [2]:




Suppose the squares of a Young diagram are filled, each with an element of the ground set of a given matroid MM, so that the rows are independent sets in MM. Can the elements in each row be rearranged so that the columns are independent?

Definition 1.



A Young diagram is wide if any subdiagram formed by a subset of its rows dominates its conjugate.





The ‘only if’ part of their conjecture can easily be shown to hold, so the conjecture is really about the ‘if’ part.
Handling this problem for general matroids is hard, since even the ‘easy’ case in which all rows of the given Young diagram have the same length is a notorious open problem known as Rota’s basis conjecture [5]. So, as in [2], we focus on the simple case of a free matroid.

A Young diagram is Latin if there is an assignment of integers to its cells so that each row ii of length lil_{i} is populated by the numbers 1,…,li1,\ldots,l_{i}, and the assignment is injective in each column. We call such an assignment a Latin filling.
Chow et al. showed that in the case of a free matroid, the Wide Partition Conjecture can be reduced to the following conjecture:



Conjecture 2.



Every wide Young diagram is Latin.

However, these results do not imply that Conjecture 2 holds for all Young diagrams with three distinct row lengths.
One of the main results of this work is a proof of Conjecture 2 for such Young diagrams:



Theorem 3.



A wide Young diagram with three distinct row lengths is Latin.
